era: Arcade / Dreamcast / Game Boy Advance / Xbox / PSP / Mobile
summary: Sega's score-attack taxi-driving series; use Dreamcast/Flycast for the first two games' original music, brands, and maps, Windows for Crazy Taxi 3, and original handheld/mobile releases for the spin-offs.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi

emulation.notes: Use VGA/upscaled Dreamcast output for the complete original home version.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High-resolution Dreamcast emulation with original licensed presentation intact

primary.why: The Dreamcast version adds the console-only Original map and Crazy Box while retaining the original licensed soundtrack and branded destinations; later HD/PSP ports lose music and/or advertising content, while the arcade original only has the arcade map.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast version on original hardware or Flycast with VGA/upscaled output; use later HD/mobile versions only for convenience.

secondary.exclusive_content: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars adds ad-hoc multiplayer modes around the Crazy Taxi/Crazy Taxi 2 content.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PSP multiplayer modes only if you want the added competitive Fare Wars content.
secondary.why: The PSP compilation removes licensed music/advertising, so it is not the main full-play version.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Sega NAOMI arcade release with the arcade city only.
all_releases.reason: skip: historically important original, but the Dreamcast version adds the Original map and Crazy Box.

all_releases.fidelity: Home version with arcade map, Original map, Crazy Box mini-games, original soundtrack, and branded destinations.
all_releases.reason: primary: best balance of completeness, original audiovisual identity, and high-quality emulation.

all_releases.fidelity: Home port after Sega moved third-party.
all_releases.reason: skip: same core game, but Dreamcast remains the cleaner original-complete route.

all_releases.fidelity: Home port with the same core content.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over Dreamcast.

all_releases.fidelity: PC port and later PC re-release route; the PC port uses a different soundtrack.
all_releases.reason: skip: higher PC convenience, but altered music makes Dreamcast the fuller original route.

all_releases.fidelity: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars port of the first game with added ad-hoc multiplayer but removed original music/advertising.
all_releases.reason: secondary: play only for the PSP-exclusive multiplayer modes.

all_releases.fidelity: HD downloadable port without the original licensed soundtrack and with altered branding.
all_releases.reason: skip: improved modern output, but less complete original presentation.

all_releases.fidelity: Xbox Live Arcade/Dreamcast Collection-era HD release without the original licensed soundtrack.
all_releases.reason: skip: convenient HD route, but less complete original presentation.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile release with the original soundtrack restored.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful official mobile route, but touch controls and mobile preservation make Dreamcast the stronger primary.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile release with the original soundtrack restored.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful official mobile route, but touch controls and mobile preservation make Dreamcast the stronger primary.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Later HD ports improve convenience/output but lose the original soundtrack and/or branded destinations; the Dreamcast version under modern emulation keeps the original identity and complete home content.

entries.remaster_caveats: HD/PSP versions have music and branding caveats; mobile versions restore the original soundtrack but are mobile-control/preservation routes.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi 2

emulation.notes: Use Flycast for the full Dreamcast version; PPSSPP only for Fare Wars multiplayer.

primary.why: Crazy Taxi 2 is a Dreamcast original with two New York-inspired cities, new drivers, Crazy Hop, and Crazy Pyramid content; the later PSP compilation adds multiplayer but removes the original licensed soundtrack/advertising.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast version on original hardware or Flycast with VGA/upscaled output; use Fare Wars only for PSP multiplayer.

secondary.exclusive_content: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars adds ad-hoc multiplayer modes to the Crazy Taxi 2 content.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PSP multiplayer modes only.
secondary.why: The PSP port compromises music/advertising and handheld performance, so it is secondary content rather than the main run.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Dreamcast release with Around Apple, Small Apple, Crazy Hop, and Crazy Pyramid.
all_releases.reason: primary: complete original version with the intended audiovisual identity.

all_releases.fidelity: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars port with added multiplayer but removed licensed soundtrack/advertising and handheld compromises.
all_releases.reason: secondary: play only for PSP-exclusive multiplayer.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Fare Wars adds multiplayer but removes the original soundtrack/ads and runs on weaker handheld hardware; Dreamcast remains the full main version.

entries.remaster_caveats: No standalone modern remaster documented; PSP compilation has licensing and performance caveats.

emulation.notes: Use the PC release if compatible; use Xbox emulation only if PC preservation is impractical.

primary.why: Crazy Taxi 3 was released on Xbox first, then arcade, then Windows; the PC route preserves the three-map package and allows the highest modern output when configured well.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on a compatible PC with modern compatibility fixes as needed; use Xbox or arcade hardware for original platform comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Original home-console release with the Glitter Oasis map and returning maps/characters from earlier entries.
all_releases.reason: skip: original home route, but Windows is the higher-output preservation target.

all_releases.fidelity: Crazy Taxi: High Roller arcade release on Sega Chihiro using the same three maps as the home version.
all_releases.reason: skip: arcade route, but no sourced exclusive content over the home/PC game.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release of the three-map Crazy Taxi 3 package.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-output documented route for the complete game.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows provides the complete three-map package with the best modern output path.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi: Catch a Ride

emulation.notes: Use mGBA for clean handheld preservation.

primary.why: Catch a Ride is the Game Boy Advance adaptation of Crazy Taxi, using the GBA-specific Rush engine and hardware-limited sprite/3D approach; it is a distinct handheld version rather than a replacement for Dreamcast.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Game Boy Advance hardware or mGBA; treat it as a handheld adaptation to sample after the Dreamcast original.

all_releases.fidelity: GBA-only adaptation with 3D environments and sprite-based vehicles/traffic.
all_releases.reason: primary: only released platform for this adaptation.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: This is a hardware-limited handheld adaptation, not the definitive way to play the original Crazy Taxi.

entries.remaster_caveats: Uses instrumental/altered music rather than the original licensed soundtrack.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi: Fare Wars

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for cleaner output; original PSP hardware is needed for authentic ad-hoc use.

primary.why: Fare Wars is a PSP compilation of Crazy Taxi and Crazy Taxi 2 with added ad-hoc multiplayer modes; it is the only non-Dreamcast route for Crazy Taxi 2, but loses the original soundtracks and advertising.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP hardware or PPSSPP, mainly for its multiplayer modes or portable Crazy Taxi 2 access.

all_releases.fidelity: PSP compilation of the first two games with added multiplayer and custom music support, but lower frame rate/loading/control caveats and removed licensed content.
all_releases.reason: primary: only platform for this compilation and its multiplayer additions.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Adds multiplayer and portable Crazy Taxi 2, but removes the original licensed soundtracks/advertising and has handheld performance compromises.

entries.remaster_caveats: Compilation/port with licensing and performance compromises, not a definitive replacement for Dreamcast.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi: City Rush

emulation.notes: Use preserved compatible mobile hardware/software only where legally available.

primary.why: City Rush is a free-to-play mobile spin-off built around lane-changing touch controls on iOS and Android; iOS is selected as the primary archival row only to keep exactly one primary platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play only if you already have access to a preserved compatible mobile install; there is no documented console/PC version.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Unity mobile release with mission-based touch driving.
all_releases.reason: primary: one of the two original mobile platforms and selected as the primary archival route.

all_releases.fidelity: Android version of the same free-to-play mobile game.
all_releases.reason: skip: same content route as iOS, selected as non-primary to preserve exactly one primary row.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Mobile service/access preservation is the main conflict; no console or offline definitive edition is documented here.

entries.remaster_caveats: Free-to-play mobile spin-off, not a mainline arcade sequel.

entries.title: Crazy Taxi Tycoon

primary.why: Crazy Taxi Tycoon, originally known as Crazy Taxi Gazillionaire, is a mobile idle/business-management spin-off released for iOS and Android and later delisted with servers offline.
primary.how_to_play: There is no reliable current official route; document via preserved mobile installs only where legally available.

all_releases.fidelity: Original mobile idle-management release.
all_releases.reason: primary: one of the two original mobile platforms and selected as the primary archival row.

all_releases.fidelity: Android version of the same mobile idle-management spin-off.
all_releases.reason: skip: same content route as iOS, selected as non-primary to preserve exactly one primary row.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The delisted/offline service state is the core preservation issue.

entries.remaster_caveats: Delisted free-to-play mobile spin-off with servers reported offline; not a playable modern route.
